summary: Ryōshū Matsushita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daishun Ueyama. He held a lecturing post at Ryukoku University (attested in 1987).
Ryōō (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He taught at Tō-ji (東寺総学) and at Kōyasan University.

Ryūjō Yamada (1895–1979) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Tokyo Imperial University and under Sylvain Lévi, he taught at Ryukoku University (~1925–1944), Tohoku University (~1944–1979), and Musashino University/Musashino Joshi Gakuin (~1960–1968).
Ryūzan Nishimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.
Rüdiger Schmitt is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1963–1965) and held a post at Saarland University from ~1972 to 2004.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at the University of Madras, he lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909), held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929), and edited the Journal of Indian History.

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at SPG College and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and later held professorships at Presidency College, Chennai, and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) worked in Indology and related fields. He was educated at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras, and worked as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1884–1888).

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at National College, Bangalore, and completed his doctorate at Ghent University under Etienne Vermeersch (1991), where he served as director (~1991–2017).
S. N. Savadi is an Indology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri (1893–1942) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and later as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan (1926–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He served as an honorary professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Srikanta Sastri (1904–1974) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, under M. H. Krishna, and held a post at the University of Mysore from ~1930 to 1966.

Saba Mahmood (1961–2018) was a religious studies and anthropology scholar who studied at the University of Washington and Stanford University. She held posts at the University of Chicago (~2000–2004) and the University of California, Berkeley (from 2004).

Sabine Löhr is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, where she was supervised by Lambert Schmithausen and worked as a graduate assistant (Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft).

Saburō Hasegawa (1906–1957) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He later taught at the American Academy of Asian Studies (~1954–1955) and held a post at California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Sachindra Kumar Maity is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham (~1953–1957) and held a post at Jadavpur University around 1958.

Sadajiro Sugiura (1871–1947) was a philosophy and Indology scholar who studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Philadelphia Divinity School. He held posts at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University.

Said Reza Huseini is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2013–2015), King's College London (~2015–2016), and Leiden University (~2017–2021).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921–1994) worked in history, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University under Mohammad Habib, he held positions at the University of Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).
